newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bangkok Land says to meet ECD payment.
newsitem.headline: Bangkok Land says to meet ECD payment.

text.p: Thai developer Bangkok Land Plc will transfer about 100 million baht ($3.84 million) to meet interest payments due on a Swiss franc Eurobond on Monday, the firm's Financial Director Joseph Lee told Reuters.
The firm issued a 400 million Swiss franc bond in January 1994, with the issue due to mature in 2001.
"In fact we will transfer money on the March 31st, they will get their money on the first as the 31st is a holiday in Switzerland," Lee told Reuters.
Several Thai property developers are facing a liquidity squeeze as the Thai real estate market has deteriorated and domestic interest rates have raised company financing costs.
In February, medium-sized Thai developer Somprasong Plc missed a $3.1 million-payment on a Eurobond, raising fears other Thai developers could default.
Bangkok Land has struggled to dispose of its huge Muang Thong Thani housing development in the north of Bangkok.

The project has recently and controversially been selected as the probable site of a new Thai parliament building, and for other possible state uses. The opposition in parliament has claimed the selection process was not transparent.
Government approval of those deals should bring Bangkok Land around five billion baht, Lee said.
"It's too early to make any concrete comments as the deals require cabinet approval and there are a lot of voices from the opposition," he said.
Bangkok Land has a further 50 million Swiss franc Eurobond, and a $150 million Eurobond outstanding.
Thai corporates have 93 eurobonds outstanding in six different currencies.
